Everyone deserves a shot at their dream. Michigan Reconnect has helped over 80,000 Michiganders 25 and up earn a tuition-free associate’s degree or skills certificate.

Let’s help even more Michiganders and expand Reconnect to every Michigander 21 and up.

Shit is expensive.

I will never stop working to lower costs for you and your family.

Our road crews are out there every day keeping Michigan moving.  Do your part: slow down, pay attention to signage, and stay alert in construction zones. Let’s keep our workers safe while they fix the damn roads.


MSP Second District (@mspmetrodet)

Good morning!

If you haven’t been paying attention, you’ll need your winter coat today. 

It is the start of National Work Zone Awareness Week. Make sure you slow down and move over as these workers fix our roads.

School librarians are a guiding light. They’re mentors, advocates, and researchers that help students spark their infinite imagination.

To every librarian in Michigan, thank you for keeping our state curious and inspired 📚

We will continue to work closely with local emergency managers over the weekend and monitor water levels across the state. Thank you to all state and local emergency responders keeping Michiganders safe.

Let’s continue to stay vigilant. We will get through this together.

Today, I'm adding seven additional counties and cities to our state of emergency declaration. This declaration will help these areas with recovery efforts as they work to clean up after severe weather damaged homes, roads, and businesses.

At a time of uncertainty, Michigan stands united in what brings us together — more housing, lower costs, and helping every child read.

We're tackling these issues at the Cadillac Chamber Breakfast and across the state to make Michigan the best place to live, work and thrive.

This is great news!  Thank you to the crews who have been working 24/7 this week to restart the hydroelectric turbine which hadn't been operational for a few years. Their heroic actions are already making a big difference to lower water levels.


MichEMHS (@MichEMHS)

#BREAKING NOW: The hydraulic dam at the Cheboygan Lock and Dam Complex is officially online. Water levels are dropping.

👍Click “follow” to ensure you see important updates. This page is the official source of emergency and disaste

New housing is making its way to Cadillac! Lakelynn Apartments is adding 252 apartments in seven new buildings. This is a BFD.

It's a sign of progress towards building more homes that families can afford. Let's keep our momentum and Build, Baby Build.

For residents in Cheboygan, Charlevoix, and Emmet County, please take extra precautions and sign up for emergency notifications at: smart911.com/smart911/ref/re…
 
If there is one thing I know about Michiganders, we are tough. We can and will get through this together.

I am at the Cheboygan Lock and Dam Complex with state and local officials who are working around the clock to keep Michiganders safe. As water levels rise, we will continue to prioritize protecting Michiganders and their property with every state resource possible.

The state will continue to coordinate with local governments and monitor the situation. I encourage everyone to stay updated and follow guidance from your local emergency manager. 

We will get through this together.￼

Today, I declared a state of emergency for 32 additional counties following severe weather that has damaged homes, roads, and businesses.

This emergency declaration will deploy additional resources to help local officials and first responders protect Michiganders and property.

Protecting Michiganders and their property is our top priority. 

With already high water levels across the state and more rain in the forecast, we will keep monitoring the situation and supporting local communities with the resources they need.

Tonight, I signed an executive order to temporarily suspend motor carrier regulations for driver hours to stabilize fuel supplies in key areas of northern Michigan. This action will support local communities, first responders, and utility crews as they work to keep people safe.

Today, we broke ground on The William Schma House, an affordable place for Michiganders to call home and get back on their feet. This housing community will give Michiganders stability and support as they rebuild their lives and imagine a future filled with possibility.
